title: This Shark Was Born Before the Steam Engine

scenes.text: There's a shark in the Arctic... that is probably older than the United States.
It's called the Greenland shark. It lives in water close to freezing...
and moves slower than you walk.
For decades, no one could tell its age. Sharks don't have the bones scientists usually count.
So in twenty sixteen, researchers looked into its eyes.
The core of the eye lens forms before birth, and never changes. Carbon dating it gave an answer.
The largest shark they studied was around four hundred years old. Give or take a century.
And it doesn't become an adult until it's about one hundred and fifty.
So the oldest ones down there were young before the steam engine... and they're still in no hurry.

sources: Nielsen, J. et al. (2016) Eye lens radiocarbon reveals centuries of longevity in the Greenland shark. Science 353(6300):702-704
